chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣalt, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a group of travelers who were on a road and were ambushed by highway robbers. Then the robbers were seized, and some of them testified for others. So he said: “Their testimony is not accepted except with a confession from the robbers, or testimony against them from others.”

key_terms.اللُّصُوصُ: the robbers or thieves involved in the crime
key_terms.بِالْإِقْرَارِ: by confession or admission from the accused themselves
key_terms.رِفْقَةٍ: a group of companions or travelers journeying together
key_terms.شَهَادَتُهُمْ: their legal testimony or witness statement
key_terms.فَقُطِعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الطَّرِيقُ: they were waylaid or attacked on the road by highway robbers

ai.seo_question: Is the testimony of captured robbers for one another accepted in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the acceptance of testimony in a case involving robbers. Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that testimony from the robbers for one another is not accepted unless supported by their own confession or by testimony from other people against them.
